Subject: LLM data-use controls and geo-routing for HealthStride pilot

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to move from POC to a paid pilot. Before we lock dates we need to validate a few privacy points so our legal & security teams can greenlight the pilot:

- A firm "no-training" commitment for tenant interactions during the pilot (HealthStride data must not be used for model improvement).
- Clear ownership/entitlements for prompts and generated responses (we own prompts; need to confirm response licensing).
- List of subprocessors (including cloud infra partners) and whether any processing occurs outside the EU.
- Evidence that we can route requests to EU-only inference nodes (and fallback behavior if capacity is exhausted).

Attached is a short PDF with our requested DPA amendments and a checklist the security team will use. Can you confirm what artifacts you can provide (attestations, inventory, routing SLA) and estimated turnaround?

Appreciate a quick reply — Alec is out of pocket next week but asked me to start the queue.

Best,
Priya

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: LLM data-use controls and geo-routing for HealthStride pilot

Hi Priya — great to hear the team's ready to proceed. Quick summary of what we can provide right away and next steps: 

1) No-training (no-model-improvement) during pilot: Yes. We can commit to a contractual no-training clause for the pilot period. Operationally we will tag HealthStride traffic at the routing layer and prevent those requests from entering our model-improvement pipelines.

2) Prompt/response entitlements: By default Redwood issues a standard output license to customers for generated content. We will include language confirming HealthStride retains rights to prompts and generated outputs during the pilot. Legal can provide a redline for your review.

3) Subprocessor inventory & evidence: I've attached our current subprocessor inventory CSV. It includes compute partners and their regions; most inference runs will be on our EU pool (Frankfurt/Amsterdam). We will also produce a short attestation describing which subprocessors will touch HealthStride data and whether any transient telemetry is sent to US services (spoiler: minimal control-plane telemetry goes to our US control plane; no customer content is sent out of EU inference nodes).

4) Geo-routing and fallback: We support policy-based routing (region pinning). For pilots we can pin to EU-only inference nodes and configure an SLA-exception policy that routes to a secondary EU pool before falling back to other regions. If you require hard block (no fallback), we can discuss added capacity or a dedicated pool.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly (legal) will produce a DPA redline with the no-training clause and output rights addendum.
- Jordan (ops) will schedule a short evidence delivery (subprocessor attestation + routing config) and share an on-call contact.
- We book a 30m call with Alec and your security team to walk the artifacts.

Can you confirm a convenient time for the call (we're available Thu/Fri mornings ET)?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
redwood.ai

Hi Priya — looping in legal. A few clarifications that help scope the contractual language: 

- Pilot duration you have in mind (we'll scope the no-train clause to the pilot period unless you want a long-term amendment).
- Types of interactions: are you expecting any support transcripts, agent-assisted chats, or asynchronous batch uploads in the pilot? The processing mode affects operational routing and the evidence artifacts we produce.

Draft plan for artifacts we can deliver within 3 business days after call:
- DPA redline with pilot-specific no-training commitment and explicit output-entitlement clause.
- Subprocessor inventory (CSV) and a 1-page attestation certifying EU-only inference processing for pinned traffic.
- Ops runbook excerpt showing how to pin traffic and the fallback policy (and an option for hard block if you want to pay for reserved capacity).

If HealthStride prefers, we can also deliver an exportability check (SFTP/HTTPS transfer options) for your retention and e-discovery workflows.

Thanks — Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
